clue.text: Money supply discovered, nothing missing

indicators.note: 'nothing missing' tells us the zero shape goes absent from the word before it

parts.note: to have discovered something is to have found it
nothing is zero, the round letter O

explanation.surface: A report on finances: a cash source has been uncovered with nothing unaccounted for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes the O (nothing) out of FOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool of money set aside for some purpose is a supply of it.

clue.text: Wiggle toes here — it may help footwear problem

indicators.note: to wiggle is to move jerkily about, so these letters are jiggled into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to someone whose shoes pinch: wiggle your toes in this, it may help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wiggle' shuffles the letters of TOES HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot-shaped block put inside a shoe keeps it from creasing or losing shape, which helps with a footwear problem.

clue.text: Wine being smuggled aboard ship in jars

indicators.note: smuggled aboard a vessel means hidden inside it, so the wine goes within the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is short for steamship
hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: Contraband wine carried on a ship in jars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jars' looks like containers for the wine, but it is the verb-turned-noun sense of jolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Jars are sudden jolts or upsets, the same thing as nasty surprises or impacts.

clue.text: Like a type of estate in trouble south of river

indicators.note: in a down entry, being south of something means being written below it

parts.note: the Indus is a great river of Pakistan
a trial is an affliction or a source of trouble

explanation.surface: A property in difficulties down south of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of' puts TRIAL below INDUS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate given over to factories and warehouses is called by this adjective, so the word describes that kind of estate.

clue.text: Revise procedure for getting clean and tidy

definitions.meaning: to go over study material again to refresh it

definitions.text: procedure for getting clean and tidy
definitions.meaning: a quick wash and grooming session

explanation.surface: Swotting up and smartening up described in one breath.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh one's knowledge is the phrasal verb, and a quick wash and tidy is the matching noun.

clue.text: Writer set up one game and another

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means turned upwards, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
Go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: An author arranges one game and then another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses the pen point in this down entry; the lone definition 'another' means a second game, following on from the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The number-calling hall pastime is a second game, following on from Go.

clue.text: Newly fitted up pad with recliner — in which one won't be this!

definitions.text: in which one won't be this!

indicators.note: something newly fitted has been put together afresh, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has fitted out their flat with a reclining chair, where they will hardly sit upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly fitted' shuffles UP PAD and RECLINER together; in a recliner one lies back, so one is not upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright at a right angle to the ground is exactly what a person lounging in a reclining chair is not.

clue.text: Goes out with hounds in county as before

definitions.meaning: rides out to chase foxes with a pack of dogs
the old abbreviation for Huntingdonshire, a former English county now part of Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Rural life: riding to hounds in a county just as in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Huntingdonshire was a small English county abolished in 1974, hence 'as before'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursues foxes on horseback, and also the short name for a former shire, both fit.

clue.text: More than one detective hustles around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into another order

explanation.surface: A plural detective bustling about the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges HUSTLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Private investigators, the plural of a word for a sleuthing person.

clue.text: Nervous in a situation where cliff may collapse?

definitions.text: in a situation where cliff may collapse?
definitions.meaning: literally standing at the brink of a crumbling cliff

explanation.surface: Feeling jittery, as anyone would perched where the cliff could give way.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being tense and jittery is also, literally, standing at a brink.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed about vehicle having to be recovered

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the colour wraps round the car

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
a coupe is a two-door car

explanation.surface: Someone red-faced about having to have their car recovered by a tow truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recovered' suggests a towed car, but it means money won back.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting back money that was lost or spent is to recoup it, a synonym of recovered.

clue.text: Opposing erstwhile bolshiness, ultimately they fall in line

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against
erstwhile means former or previous

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the last letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Former rebels who once opposed everything finally toe the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letter, S, of 'bolshiness'.
explanation.definitionFit: People who comply with rules and norms are said to fall in line, as conformists do.

clue.text: Four daring to go wild in place of entertainment

indicators.note: going wild means running riot, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Four thrill-seekers running riot at an amusement venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go wild' shuffles FOUR DARING.
explanation.definitionFit: A site with rides and sideshows set up for amusement is a place of entertainment.

clue.text: Some statement issued by benefactor of art

indicators.note: some of a word is only part of it, so the letters sit inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A press release put out by an arts patron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals letters found inside STATEMENT. Henry Tate, the sugar magnate, founded the London gallery bearing his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugar merchant who funded a famous London gallery is a well-known benefactor of art.

clue.text: I paid sentries for working — people getting regular payments

indicators.note: working here means being worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who paid guards for their work, salaried people all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' shuffles I PAID SENTRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who receive a fixed stipend or salary are people getting regular payments.

clue.text: Dirty location near Heathrow almost changed finally

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the town comes off

parts.note: Staines is a town in Surrey close to London's main airport

indicators.note: finally points to the end letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A grubby place beside Heathrow has nearly been changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final S from STAINES; 'finally' takes D, the end of 'changed'. Heathrow is London's biggest airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marked with spots or blotches is soiled, that is dirty.

clue.text: Provide machinery for chum getting under car

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting under means placed below, so the friend follows the car

parts.note: auto is short for automobile
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend crawls under a car to fix it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting under' puts MATE below AUTO in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To mechanise a process is to equip it with machines so it runs by itself.

clue.text: Go in Scotland in criminal group

definitions.meaning: the Scots dialect verb meaning to go or walk

explanation.surface: Visiting Scotland among a mob of villains.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots use the word for walking or going, and it also means a band of criminals.

clue.text: Competitor cheated dreadfully, having got let in

indicators.note: in means put inside, so the given word goes within the jumbled letters
done dreadfully means done badly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An athlete who cheated badly and was still allowed into the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' scrambles the letters to DECATHE before 'in' inserts the given word; 'Competitor' sounds like the cheat, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete taking part in a ten-event contest is a competitor.

clue.text: Mother comes with a loaf of bread

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
per means a, as in 'pounds per hour' for pounds an hour

explanation.surface: Mum arrives carrying a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Damper is an Australian bush bread, a simple soda loaf baked in campfire ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian unleavened soda bread cooked in embers is a type of loaf.

clue.text: Singer sounding note

indicators.note: sounding means as heard spoken, so the money word stands for one pronounced the same

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: A vocalist hitting a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests music, but it is a banknote: a tenner is a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A man with a high adult voice is a type of singer in a choir.

clue.text: Unofficial instruction to tell a student what is going on

parts.note: inform is the command to tell someone something
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: An off-the-record order to brief a pupil on events.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'instruction to tell a student what is going on' as INFORM A L: an order to tell a learner the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual or not done through formal channels, the same as unofficial.

clue.text: Time when soldiers will get involved in test

indicators.note: getting involved in something means going inside it, so the soldiers go within the test

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles
men are ordinary soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A point when troops will be caught up in a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: MOT is Britain's yearly compulsory vehicle safety check.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief instant or particular point is a time, as in 'at that time'.

clue.text: Most significant European river

definitions.meaning: the ... flows through Frankfurt in Germany

explanation.surface: The most important river in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for chief or principal is also a German river joining the Rhine.

clue.text: Poet's appointment around noon

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the meeting wraps round the abbreviation

parts.note: a date is a fixed meeting

explanation.surface: A poet has a midday meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' means Poet is, the 's linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine author of the Divine Comedy is a famous Italian poet.

clue.text: King wanting new attire, becoming more annoyed

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the clothing word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch who lacks new clothes grows crosser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the clothing word to give the letters ATTIER; 'wanting' is a link meaning needing, not a deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British slang for irritable, so its comparative means crosser or more annoyed.
